completion_data.completion_summary: Requirement (S) of the ray-product verdict is landed: a finite labelled presentation satisfying the eleven-field consistency bundle Cons is realized by a regular Z-model constructed from it (presented_modelOf), and the realized set of that model's seam IS the computable hitOf of the presentation at every depth k >= 1 (hitCl_modelOf_eq_hitOf) -- HWZ 2000 Theorem 14 in the (<=) direction for the box-dot fibre. Scope, carried in the statements rather than in prose: box/stab-free phi of L+, ONE seam, [F.IsRegular] via frameOf_isRegular, [Fintype Q] on the PRESENTATION only (the constructed model's carrier Z x Q is infinite, so no finite-fibre or finite-width assumption is introduced). Probe735.not_presented is neither refuted nor weakened: it quantifies over models not built from a presentation, and both wired probes stay. The box/stab-bearing fragment and the lift from one seam to validity are assigned to requirement (W); Decidable (PlusValidZTime phi) is not stated in any form and no complexity bound is claimed. The carried 300-500 line frame-constructor prerequisite was descoped on a machine-checked finding that (S) does not need it, and remeasured at ~120-160 lines as a parallel constructor, with the branching probe holding both its positive bound and its two refutations of the obvious repair shapes.

memory_candidates: In Lean 4, `omit [Inst] in` must be the INNERMOST modifier in a suppression stack: placed above the `set_option ... in` lines it silently stops those options reaching the declaration, and placed between a `--` reason comment and its suppression it makes the suppression read as unreasoned to a checker whose walk-back pattern matches `set_option ... in` only.

A blanket file-level `set_option linter.X false` and an env_linter batch finding are different problems with different fixes: the `set_option` hides only LSP-side linters, so an `unusedArguments` finding survives it and needs either an `omit` (which removes the binder) or a nolints entry. Prefer `omit` -- but it cascades: dropping a binder from a helper can push the same finding up to its callers.

When a theorem-index row's Axioms cell claims `pinned:<check>`, that is an assertion the check actually makes -- verify the declaration is in the check's baseline before writing the cell, or the row documents a pin nobody enforces.

A Lean project whose `defaultTargets` names only the main library is not fully verified by `lake build`: a test library's `#guard`/`#guard_msgs` are never elaborated until that library is built by name.
